question: From 20 April to 21 June 2026, the Commission ran the campaign ‘Protect what matters: our democracy’ (with the involvement of the agencies Havas Paris, Havas Play, Havas Media, Prose on Pixels), securing over 75 440 outdoor advertising spaces in 3 650 cities across all 27 Member States.

In statements to the media, the European Commission representation in Estonia quoted figures of approximately EUR 3 million for content creation and production and EUR 30 million for media placement, adding that a breakdown by Member State would not provide a complete picture. 1.
Can the Commission confirm or correct the sums quoted and can it indicate the budget line used, with a breakdown by type of expenditure and by Member State?
If the Commission deems it impossible to provide a country-by-country breakdown, can it say why a campaign of this magnitude can dispense with country-by-country cost transparency?

Can the Commission specify when, and pursuant to which legal instrument, the decision was taken to undertake the campaign, and under which contractual framework (framework agreement, dynamic purchasing system, specific contract) the agencies involved were engaged?
